status: PRE-REGISTERED 2026-11-14 before running mi.model.evaluate. Do not edit after the first run; write v2 instead.
question: Does any purposeful candidate improve decision-relevant ranking/calibration of 4-week category purchase over the production model (hgb_small) and the baselines?

candidates.rule_repeat: weeks with a category purchase in the last 12 weeks, ties by recency (baseline)
candidates.logreg_l2: regularised logistic regression on the production features (log1p + standardise)
candidates.hgb_small_longhist: hgb_small + 3 longer-history features computed from weeks <= cutoff only: cat_weeks_active_prior14 (weeks cutoff-25..cutoff-12), cat_bought_before_lookback (any purchase before the 12-week lookback), history_weeks_available. Motivation: the documented failure on households with no recent category history.

splits.note_49: Window 49 has been inspected in earlier passes; results on it are REPEATED evaluation, not an untouched test.
splits.rolling_origin: for target cutoffs 41, 45, 49 refit each candidate on all cutoffs c with c + 4 <= target (labels fully observed before the target cutoff)

adoption_rule: Replace hgb_small only if a candidate improves AP by >= 0.005 on the selection window 41 AND on the rolling-origin window 45, AND does not lower AP on the no-recent-history subgroup (LOW_ACTIVITY + ACTIVE_NONBUYER) at window 41. Otherwise keep hgb_small and report the negative result.
metrics: Brier and ECE after isotonic calibration fit on window 45 (evaluated on 49)
precision/recall at the top 5/10/20% of rows
precision/recall per category at k = 250 households
household-cluster bootstrap (200 draws) CI of AP(model) - AP(rule) for slices with >= 100 positives
intended_use: ranking existing households by probability of buying a category under historical conditions; NOT coupon uplift or persuadability
